status: UI design baseline; app implementation and runtime validation remain future gates.

consultation.isolation: No tools, no MCP servers, safe mode, no Chrome, no skills, plan permission mode and no persisted Claude session. Only the supplied public/source-reviewed context was sent.

recommendation.name_status: Dedicated repository Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-leaderboard is selected; PickYour.AI Credits remains a proposed product name requiring the design decision.
recommendation.visual_direction: An editorial contribution ledger, with equal-weight departments, precise tabular numbers, hairline rules and clear source proof.
core_decisions: Recognize many distinct kinds of work through parallel boards and an inclusive contributor directory.
Do not create an overall contributor score, streak pressure, an inactivity list or an employee performance comparison.
Every displayed metric must have a defined unit, eligible population, date basis, coverage and public evidence path.
People can inspect submitted and observed work even when no accepted outcome has occurred.
Code volume is a visible optional dimension with context; it does not dominate the homepage.
Browsing is anonymous; authentication is optional and reserved for verified preferences and correction administration.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus treats labels present for 14 days as Accepted, and proposes a 30-day duplicate window.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Persistence is an observable maturity signal, not proof of correctness or acceptance. Use Observed or Matured labels unless a separate reviewed outcome exists. Any window is versioned policy, not a discovered requirement; never delay all credit for a newcomer solely because of a window.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus describes issues closed as completed as Accepted reports.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Show precise observable states such as Issues closed as completed. A closure reason alone does not certify a useful report, research completion, a verified fix or deployment. Outcome-specific boards require their own evidence.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: One example ranks 31 labels while 28 are accepted and 3 are provisional under accepted scope.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: The rank value must use only the selected eligible state. Show accepted 28 and provisional 3 separately. Never silently add incompatible states or units.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus directory eligibility requires an accepted receipt.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Include everyone with a verifiable eligible public contribution, including observed submissions, issue diagnosis and review. State filters may narrow the directory, but initial acceptance delays must not erase contributors. Assignment or membership alone is not a contribution.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus uses one global accepted-date default.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: The global scope is a requested view, while each metric declares supported state and date bases. Do not invent an acceptance timestamp for an observed label, comment or structural link. Show incompatible choices explicitly and select the metric's declared default.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus suggests coauthor email mapping as verification.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: A trailer or matching email alone is insufficient. Use documented reliable account attribution and verified person-account coauthor evidence. The observed Claude Opus 5.5 trailer is AI-assistance metadata and must not create a human leaderboard identity. Never publish linking emails.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus proposes bulk revert-and-exclude for triage spam.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Administrative actions affect only this leaderboard's inclusion records and reversible credit decisions. Never silently edit or revert upstream GitHub labels, issue state, relationships or Project fields.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus proposes showing a named contributor's opt-out in public microcopy.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Avoid exposing privacy choices unnecessarily. Honor suppression across profile, board, wall, export, search and share assets; publish only a minimal generic redacted correction record when appropriate. Define aggregate behavior before rollout.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus proposes 100-row pagination plus Show all.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Use accessible bounded pagination and server/snapshot-filtered export. Offer Show all only below a documented safe result cap; do not create an unbounded DOM or download.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus suggests a live cross-repository token drift CI dependency.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Keep a versioned local token contract with the source SHA and an explicit update workflow. Detect divergence without making every remote website styling change an uncontrolled build dependency.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus reserves amber for changes and forbids red/green globally.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Preserve restrained teal/slate/amber branding and neutral ranking. Semantic validation or destructive controls may use accessible status colors with words/icons; do not confuse rank with correctness. Always label states rather than relying on glyph or color.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus proposes a commenter contacting the owner of open ASCII work.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Record future coordination with website #32/#33 in the plan. This concept phase sends no comments or messages. Current user authorization does not require implementation or contact now.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus coverage examples include full since repository creation.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Use that claim only after a documented completeness check for the precise source and metric. A successful pagination pass does not establish that GitHub retained every historical action. Unknown and unavailable remain distinct from zero.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus rank comparison example does not constrain changing policy or populations.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Show changes only for comparable date windows, eligible populations, attribution policy and coverage. Otherwise state Comparison unavailable because the scope or method changed.

reviewed_amendments_to_opus.finding: Opus describes static wall mode as refreshing periodically.
reviewed_amendments_to_opus.decision: Distinguish frozen snapshot, single-board auto-refresh and cycling live modes in the configurator. A frozen snapshot never changes and says so. Live modes apply data only at safe update boundaries.

information_architecture.separate_actor_area: Automation; main area is user-account activity, not a claim of manually performed work
scope_rules: Use stable IDs internally; names are display values and may change.
Research T0-T6 is not the whole organization's program taxonomy.
Website, Android and Apple programs may share a repository.
A contribution may belong to multiple programs but counts once in an organization aggregate.
Unknown or unassigned program remains visible without inferred membership.
Invalid or incompatible filters get a visible explanation, not silent substitution.
Default period is the last 30 days. Support 7/30/90-day rolling windows, all-time, custom half-open UTC windows and calendar presets including quarter.
Public actor filters say user accounts, automation and all activity. An event attributed to a person account does not prove manual execution or absence of AI assistance.

screen_behavior.overview: Show all departments with the same visual weight and a clear explainable lead metric. Lead metrics prefer verifiable outcomes, but departments without an outcome metric show a clearly labeled observed measure or availability explanation. Never fabricate an accepted state to fill a slot. Keep the People link and unranked first-contribution strip visible. Unsupported departments remain discoverable.
screen_behavior.board: Header states measure, unit, period, date basis, actor scope, method version and coverage. Hold updates by default. Use a semantic table with contextual columns. An explicit contributor link opens a shareable proof drawer; a separate profile link remains a normal navigation target. Accepted and provisional values never share a rank numerator. Pending evidence is distinct from unsupported source capability, partial history, stale collection and unknown actor. None of those states is automatically a zero or an accepted outcome.
screen_behavior.ties: Use shared dense ranks 1, =2, =2, 3. Alphabetical/ID display within ties has no rank or credit effect. Top-N boundaries include tied contributors or provide explicit continuation. Small-cohort presentation and threshold are versioned policy choices; retain visible counts and do not invent inferior ranks.
screen_behavior.loc: Expose additions, deletions, net, changed files, PR count and PR-size context separately. Group source/docs/tests/generated/vendor/lockfile/other. Show bulk import, formatting and rename exclusions with exact classifier coverage. Do not use net LOC as a default merit ranking or code volume as the Overview lead.
screen_behavior.profile: Group measures by department, with no total score. Show evidence links, selected scope, verified roles, first observed contribution with coverage caveat and optional consented highlights. Distinguish no eligible activity from not measured. No public linking emails or inferred private work. Optional monthly summaries require complete enough data and an accessible table.
screen_behavior.proof: Show the exact observed action and actor role, activity/acceptance timestamps where applicable, current policy inclusion, public source, ingestion provenance, correction history and exclusion reason. GitHub author, merger, reviewer and closer are distinct roles. A missing actor does not become an assumed assignee.
screen_behavior.methodology: Each method contains what counts, unit, numerator/denominator, population, date basis, tie semantics, exclusions, sources, coverage, known gaps, gaming risks and policy version. Keep concise method disclosure on the board itself.
screen_behavior.coverage: Accessible repository/source/metric matrix and mobile per-repository list. Display history boundaries and outages, current freshness and attribution gaps. Avoid completeness percentages when the denominator is unknowable.
screen_behavior.corrections: Every proof offers a prefilled issue-form link for public factual corrections, with snapshot and receipt IDs. Sensitive privacy requests require a verified staffed private path before public launch; do not invent an email address or claim a nonfunctional form works. Later authenticated tools show preview, reason and reversible internal application.

design_system.typography: Existing system sans for body and navigation; existing monospace with tabular numerals for metrics. Opus proposes Instrument Serif for page titles only; adopting it is optional and requires license verification, self-hosted subset, no-font fallback and a layout-shift check.
design_system.layout: Hairline separators rather than a field of cards; 1280px default content max; spacing 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64; mobile starts at 320px reflow with 16px side padding; 640/1024/1280 layout changes.
design_system.density: 44px comfortable row targets; compact mode only for fine pointers and sufficient viewport, retaining usable interactive targets.
design_system.drawer: 480px supplementary panel on desktop, full-screen dialog below 1024px; focus placement, Escape, focus return and back navigation are defined.
design_system.evidence_glyphs: Optional symbols accompany persistent text labels. No color-only or glyph-only meaning; no unsupported claim that glyphs alone guarantee accessibility.
design_system.ascii_coordination: Current #32/#33 proposals are unmerged and local-only. Reserve an optional empty decorative slot; do not create a dependency on their code. Any future artwork must be aria-hidden, bounded, pausable, responsive, reduced-motion aware and paused offscreen.

accessibility_and_resilience: WCAG 2.2 AA acceptance target, measured contrast, keyboard support, semantic headings and tables, visible unobscured focus and skip navigation.
Verify with keyboard and at least two representative screen readers; test 200% text/zoom, 400% reflow as appropriate and 320px CSS width.
Use one polite live summary per applied batch. Do not announce each changed row or move focus automatically on background refresh.
Tables retain captions, row/column headers and aria-sort; mobile stacked layouts preserve programmatic relationships.
All charts have adjacent text/table equivalents; use explicit units and Intl formatting with visible UTC cutoff semantics.
Support reduced motion, forced colors, no custom font, missing avatar, slow network, stale snapshot and failed refresh.
Optional single-key shortcuts are discoverable and can be disabled; do not intercept text entry.
Sanitize any rendered public source text, validate external source URLs, and export CSV safely against formula injection.
Provide independent light/dark/system preference without requiring account creation or tracking.
Synthetic fixtures are clearly named and carry a persistent banner on every route; they cannot silently enter public production datasets.
Use precise user-account versus automation labels; keep execution mode and declared AI assistance as independent evidence fields, never infer them from a GitHub account type.

live_display.read_mode: Hold while I read is default. Queue new snapshots and show an Apply updates control. Preserve filter state, scroll, selection and focus.
live_display.follow_mode: Explicit opt-in. No reordering while keyboard focus, pointer engagement or proof drawer is active. Apply coherent snapshots at safe intervals. No partial mix of policy/snapshot numerators and denominators.
live_display.freshness: Show data-as-of timestamp, observation/ingestion freshness and reconciliation status distinctly. Labels are Fresh, Polling, Delayed, Reconciling, Stale or Error based on verified pipeline metadata, not a decorative always-green live indicator.
live_display.wall_defaults: 30-second cycle, minimum proposed 20 seconds, avatars off, safe margins, persistent scope and freshness, no marquee or count-up effects. Reduced motion uses instant transitions.
live_display.wall_controls: Pause/play, previous/next, cycle interval, display mode and motion setting. Configurator copies a public URL and never automatically launches OBS or external software.
live_display.fair_exposure: Cycle configured departments and tie continuation pages transparently. Offer an unranked contributor credits roll so high-volume contributors are not the only people ever displayed.
live_display.privacy: Public eligible data only, no private Project metadata, no restricted evidence or identity emails. Respect contributor display suppression on every generated wall payload.
